# Spacedock

> Your agents are waiting on you. Spacedock brings you the calls that need you, keeps your agents on the goal, and lets you decide in one place.

Documentation for Spacedock, which runs inside your existing coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, or Pi) and has three features. Spacedock Review puts your agent's work in front of you and sends your comments back. Spacedock Compass shows whether your agents are still on the goal. Spacedock Workflow breaks work into stages and surfaces an evidenced decision at each gate. This index links the product docs; llms-full.txt is every page concatenated into one file for a single fetch.

# Get started

# Your agents need your judgement

Keeping up with their work takes attention. Spacedock brings plans and drafts to you for review. It helps you and your agents keep your goals on track, and lets you define which decisions need you.

## Quick start

Paste this into your agent:

`Install Spacedock using https://spacedock.md/agents.md and use Spacedock Review for plans and artifacts I need to review.` copy

[Manual installation](get-started/install/).

## Your attention bottlenecks

Your attention goes into judging work, keeping goals on track and setting the standards agents work to.

- **[Review](review/):** Bring the work and evidence together when you need to make a call.
- **[Compass](compass/):** Check where your agents' work stands against your goals.
- **[Workflow](workflow/):** Define what needs your judgement and refine it as trust grows.

# Installation

Spacedock works with Claude Code and Codex.

## Install Spacedock

`brew trust spacedock-dev/tap brew install --cask spacedock-dev/tap/spacedock` copy

`curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/spacedock-dev/spacedock/main/install.sh | sh export PATH="${SPACEDOCK_INSTALL_DIR:-$HOME/.local/bin}:$PATH"` copy

The installer looks up releases at `spacedock.md` with User-Agent `spacedock-install/<version|unknown> (<os>; <arch>[; ci][; internal])`. The version identifies the installed Spacedock binary. If the version probe fails or takes more than two seconds, the installer uses `unknown`. The installer uses GitHub directly if the route fails or takes more than five seconds.

PostHog counts each lookup without the caller's IP address. Plausible uses the caller's IP address to count the lookup but does not store it. CI lookups are not counted. The installer adds `; ci` when `CI` is `1`, `true`, `yes`, or `on`, regardless of case or surrounding whitespace. Set `SPACEDOCK_INTERNAL=1` to add `; internal`.

## Set up your agent

`spacedock install --host claude` copy

Run `/reload-plugins` or start a new session.

`spacedock install --host codex` copy

Start a new session.

## Confirm setup

`spacedock doctor` copy

In Codex, run `spacedock doctor --host codex`. Follow the instructions in the doctor output.

## Keep it up to date

Run `spacedock update`. It updates Spacedock, Review, Compass and their plugins together. A Homebrew install prints the `brew upgrade` command to run instead.

[Your first review](../../review/use/).
# Review

# Spacedock Review

More agent work means more decisions for you. Review plans, drafts and reports, then decide what happens next.

## Your decision

Select text to leave a comment, then make the call:

- **Approve:** the agent can proceed.
- **Request changes:** ask the agent to revise.
- **Hold decision:** pause the work.

Your agent picks up your feedback and acts on your decision. No need to copy it back into the conversation.

## Local and hosted

Review beside your agent. The document stays on your machine. Leave comments and approve, request changes or hold the work.

[Supported terminals and controls](terminal/)

[review.spacedock.md](https://review.spacedock.md) is Spacedock’s hosted review service, free with [limits](reference/#limits). Create an account and pair your computer for higher limits.

People you invite can comment through the link you share with them.

## How it works

Each agent that asked for a review waits for its own result, the way its tool (Claude Code or Codex) waits.

When you finish, the result contains your decision, anchored comments and the document version you reviewed, and it goes back to the conversation that asked. Claude Code and Codex wait differently, but receive the same result.

**Related guides**

- [Your first review](use/): send your own plan, leave feedback and read the agent’s response.
- [Comments and decisions](decisions/): what each decision means.
- [Sharing](sharing/): invite others before you make the call.
- [Spacedock Workflow](../concepts/gates-and-decisions/): define what needs your judgement and what evidence each review presents.

# Browser review

Review your agent’s work in your browser. Spacedock hosts the uploaded document; your agent stays in its existing environment.

## Open your review

In Claude Code, request a decision in the browser:

`/spacedock:review plan.md web decision` copy

In Codex, use `$spacedock:review` with the same arguments.

Or ask your agent:

> Send plan.md to me in Spacedock Review in the browser for a decision.

Agree to the upload. The first time, your agent runs `subspace-relay-client pair` for you to pair this computer with your account: sign in and approve in the browser page it opens. You pair once per computer.

Over SSH, the terminal shows a link and a code instead. Open the link in a browser on any device, sign in, enter the code and approve. Then confirm in the terminal: answer `y`. If your agent started the pairing and reports `paired: not yet`, run `subspace-relay-client pair --confirm` in your own terminal on that computer and answer `y` there.

Your agent then opens the review. Signed in, you are the owner and make the decision. Send the same share link to [invite others](../sharing/); they comment, and only you decide.

## Comment and decide

1. Select text and add a comment.
1. Press **Finish review**. Choose **Approve**, **Request changes** or **Hold decision**.
1. Press **Send decision**. Your agent receives the decision and included comments. The review closes.

Comments you have added are included automatically; add or cancel any text still in the comment box first. For comments already sent, select **Include** beside each one you want returned with your decision.

To send comments while keeping the review open, choose **Send comments, leave open**. You can decide later.

**Related guides**

- [Sharing](../sharing/)
- [Comments and decisions](../decisions/)
- [Link expiry and waiting limits](../reference/#limits)

# Comments and decisions

A comment identifies something to discuss or change. A decision tells your agent whether to continue, revise or stop.

| Decision            | What happens next                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Approve**         | The agent continues the task within the permission you already gave it                                                                                                              |
| **Request changes** | In the browser, the agent revises the file using your feedback and shares it again. In the terminal, the agent receives your feedback and acts within the permission it already has |
| **Hold decision**   | The agent pauses the work                                                                                                                                                           |

A decision closes the review. Comments alone do not mean approval.

Your decision can include comments. In a shared review, invited reviewers can comment. Only you, as the owner, make the decision.

**Related guides**

- [Terminal decisions](../terminal/#make-a-decision)
- [Browser decisions](../browser/#comment-and-decide)
- [Workflow gates](../../concepts/gates-and-decisions/)

# Review reference

## Review requests

Use `/spacedock:review` in Claude Code or `$spacedock:review` in Codex. Both use the same arguments. Replace `plan.md` with your file name.

| Arguments                                      | What happens                                                            |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `plan.md terminal decision`                    | Review in the terminal and make a decision                              |
| `plan.md web decision`                         | Review in the browser and make a decision, after agreeing to the upload |
| `plan.md decision`                             | Make a decision using your project's saved review location              |
| `plan.md terminal questions`                   | Review in the terminal with questions enabled                           |
| `plan.md`                                      | Review the file using your project's saved location                     |
| `terminal`                                     | Save Terminal as this project's preference                              |
| `web`                                          | Save Web as this project's preference, after agreeing to uploads        |
| No arguments                                   | View or change this project's preference                                |
| A prompt, such as `draft release notes for v2` | Ask the agent to carry it out, then review the resulting file           |

A location supplied with a file applies to that review only. Without a saved preference, your agent asks where to review.

To save a preference, `terminal` also accepts `tui` or `local`, and `web` also accepts `webui` or `remote`. With a file, use `terminal` or `web` exactly.

Or ask your agent:

> Send plan.md to me in Spacedock Review for a decision.

## Terminal keys

| Key     | Action                                                        |
| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `c`     | Comment on selected text                                      |
| `s`     | Suggest replacement text                                      |
| `Q`     | Ask the agent a question when questions are enabled           |
| `R`     | Refresh the answer to your latest question                    |
| `T`     | Set an automatic answer refresh interval; press again to stop |
| `q`     | Finish, or open the decision screen                           |
| `Tab`   | Choose a decision on the finish screen                        |
| `Enter` | Send the decision, or save the note you are editing           |
| `Esc`   | Leave the finish screen, or discard the note you are editing  |
| `?`     | Show all keys                                                 |

## Review modes

| Mode       | Result                            |
| ---------- | --------------------------------- |
| `feedback` | Comments                          |
| `binding`  | Comments and the owner's decision |

A plain terminal file review defaults to `feedback`. The `decision` keyword requests `binding` mode.

Your agent receives `approve`, `revise` or `hold` for Approve, Request changes and Hold decision. See [Comments and decisions](../decisions/) for what each means.

## Agent commands

Installing Spacedock adds `subspace-relay-client`; a Homebrew install also names it `rr`, which the table uses. After a curl install, type `subspace-relay-client` in place of `rr`. Your agent runs these for you.

| Command                                   | Action                                                                                        |
| ----------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `rr pair`                                 | Pair this computer with your account, once; you sign in and approve in your browser           |
| `rr publish <file> --open`                | Upload the file, print its share link and open it in your browser                             |
| `rr decision <share-url> --with-included` | Wait for the owner's decision and included comments                                           |
| `rr feedback <share-url>`                 | Read the review's comments and decisions from the publishing machine                          |
| `rr revoke <share-url>`                   | Revoke access through the share link                                                          |
| `rr device`                               | Check whether this computer is paired with an account                                         |
| `rr unpair`                               | Unpair this computer. Share links keep working; you decide on its reviews again after pairing |

Use `--timeout` with `rr decision` to set the wait duration, for example `--timeout 110m`.

Your paired computers are listed at `review.spacedock.md/account/computers`, where you can remove one.

## Limits

| Limit                             | Value                                                   |
| --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| Share link                        | Seven days from sharing by default                      |
| Automatic wait in Claude Code     | Up to 110 minutes                                       |
| Automatic wait in Codex           | Up to 12 hours                                          |
| Shares per day, unpaired computer | 5                                                       |
| Shares per day, paired computer   | 100 per computer and 100 across the account's computers |
| File size                         | 1 MB per share                                          |
| Feedback sends                    | 100 per reviewer session, 200 per review                |

# Shared reviews

Invite others to comment before you decide. Send them the **share link** from your browser review; they comment, and only you decide.

## Reviewer access

Reviewers open the link, select text and comment. They need nothing installed and can use an anonymous name or sign in.

You see everyone’s comments. Each reviewer sees only their own. A reviewer can also give the link to their agent to leave feedback; it reads review.spacedock.md/llms.txt and comments under the name it declares.

## Make the call

Signed in as the owner, select **Include** beside the comments you want your agent to receive. Then [send your decision](../browser/#comment-and-decide).

Only the owner decides. Finishing with a decision closes the review to further comments.

## Document access

Spacedock’s hosted service stores the uploaded document, comments and decision. Anyone holding the share link can read the entire document, so share it only with people who should have access.

Share links expire after seven days by default. [Review the limits](../reference/#limits) and create an account and pair your computer for higher limits. Ask your agent to [revoke the link](../reference/#commands-your-agent-runs-for-web-reviews) to end access sooner. For example: "Revoke the share link for plan.md."

**Related guides**

- [Browser review](../browser/)
- [Link and account limits](../reference/#limits)

# Terminal review

Review beside your agent in tmux, Zellij, Herdr or cmux, or in a Ghostty or Apple Terminal window. The file stays on your machine.

## Open the review

In Claude Code, request a decision in the terminal:

`/spacedock:review plan.md terminal decision` copy

In Codex, use `$spacedock:review` with the same arguments.

`terminal` is optional. Omit it to use your project's saved preference. To save Terminal for this project, run `/spacedock:review terminal`.

Or ask your agent:

> Open plan.md in Spacedock Review in the terminal and ask for my decision.

## Comment or suggest an edit

Select text, then press `c` to comment or `s` to suggest replacement text.

## Finish the review

Press `q` to open the finish screen. Press `Tab` to choose **Approve**, **Request changes** or **Hold decision**, then `Enter` to send.

Request changes and Hold decision need a comment, a suggested edit or an overall note. Your agent receives your decision and comments.

## Questions

In Claude Code, open the terminal review with questions enabled:

`/spacedock:review plan.md terminal questions` copy

Or ask your agent:

> Open plan.md in Spacedock Review in the terminal with questions enabled.

Answers appear beside the document and use the agent's original conversation context.

Press `Q` to ask a question, such as "What's next?"

Press `T`, enter an interval in minutes, then `Enter` to refresh the answer automatically. Press `T` again to stop.

**Related guides**

- [Comments and decisions](../decisions/)
- [Terminal keys](../reference/#terminal-keys)
- [Workflow gates](../../concepts/gates-and-decisions/)

# Your first review

[Install Spacedock](../../get-started/install/). In Claude Code, use the review skill. Replace `plan.md` with your file name:

`/spacedock:review plan.md decision` copy

In Codex, use `$spacedock:review` with the same arguments.

Or ask your agent:

> Send plan.md to me in Spacedock Review for a decision.

No active plan right now? Try this:

`Based on my recent agent history, draft a concise recommendation on whether we should adopt Spacedock Review. Use /spacedock:review to send it to me for a decision.` copy

## Open the review

Choose **Terminal** to review on your machine, or **Web** to review in your browser. Your agent remembers the choice for this project.

For Web, agree to the upload the first time in a project. The first time on a computer, your agent runs `subspace-relay-client pair` for you to pair this computer with your account: sign in and approve in your browser. After that, your agent opens the review and you decide while signed in.

## Add a comment

Select the text you want changed.

- **Terminal:** press `c` to add a comment.
- **Browser:** type your comment in the box that opens.

## Finish the review

- **Approve** to let your agent continue.
- **Request changes** to send the work back with your feedback.

Press `q` to open the finish screen. Press `Tab` to choose your decision, then `Enter` to send.

Press **Finish review**, choose your decision, then **Send decision**.

Your agent receives your comments and decision automatically.

**Related guides**

- [Comments and decisions](../decisions/): what happens after your decision.
- [Terminal controls and approval requests](../terminal/)
- [Browser review](../browser/)
- [Sharing](../sharing/)
# Compass

# What is Spacedock Compass

You give an agent a goal and go do something else. Twenty turns later it is rewriting a file you never mentioned, or it has declared the work done and it isn't. With several sessions running, you find out when you read the result. **Compass keeps the goal you set beside what each session is doing, so the session that has left it stands out while it is still running.**

## How it works

Compass is a screen on your own machine that lists every agent session you have running, across Claude Code, Codex and eight other agent tools. For each active session it shows where the work is, what the agent is doing now, what it does next, and whether it is blocked.

*Each active session shows its goal beside what the agent is doing. Sessions with a recorded departure carry a Drift mark and sit above ordinary working sessions, below sessions waiting on you or holding a question.*

This is **Intent and drift**. You state your intent for a session as a goal. A `/goal` you set in Claude Code, Codex or Antigravity becomes the goal on its own. When you ask, Compass [checks the session against that intent](use/#check-a-session-for-drift) and says where the agent departed, citing the exact entries in the session record. When Claude Code or Codex says a goal is met, Compass displays the claim; Analyze drift checks it against what the session recorded. You decide what to do about a departure: tell the agent, adjust the intent, or leave it. Treat a drift level as an account of the evidence, not a measurement.

Compass reads your agents' session files and never writes to them. It never types into a session or chooses an answer for you; when a session asks through Compass, it returns the option you select. It keeps its own notes, your intent and a short history of what it observed, on your machine. With Compass on its default local address, session content leaves your machine only through model calls: [Analyze drift](use/#check-a-session-for-drift), session summaries, [Live monitor](use/#watch-a-session-live), and [checks Compass runs on its own](use/#let-compass-check-while-you-are-away). Calls run when you press a control or enable a feature. Opening a finished Claude Code session can start a missing summary, with summaries enabled and within its limits. The first of each kind tells you what it sends and where. **Pause model calls** stops all of them, and `--no-observer-model` refuses them for a whole run. Compass also reads your Claude Code and Cursor quota, which sends no session content; turn it off on the Sessions screen or with `--no-usage`.

## With Workflow

If you run work through [Spacedock Workflow](../workflow/), Compass also shows which step each work item is in and the decisions Workflow recorded for it. It can [alert you once](use/#get-alerted-when-work-reaches-a-step) when an item reaches a step you pick.

## When to use it

- You run more than one agent session and cannot watch them all.
- You step away during long runs and want to know, on return, which sessions need you.
- Your review comments keep saying "this isn't what we agreed".

## Next

- **Set your first intent.** [Install Spacedock](../#install), then [state an intent for a session and check it for drift](use/#set-the-goal).
- **Then Workflow.** If drift keeps coming from work that was never pinned down, [Spacedock Workflow](../workflow/) lets you write down once what good looks like at each step.
- [Compass reference](reference/): commands, options and keys.
# Workflow, what it is

# Spacedock Workflow

Your agents can do more work than you can review. Spacedock Workflow lets you define what needs your attention and what agents can handle themselves.

## How it works

A workflow gives recurring work a set of stages, such as design, implementation and review. You define the standards for each stage. Agents choose how to do the work within those standards.

You also choose where work pauses for your decision. These checkpoints are called [gates](../concepts/gates-and-decisions/).

The stages and standards live in plain text in your repository. Your agent coordinates the work and records its progress and decisions.

## Gate content

Different stages need different context and evidence for your judgment. **Gate content** defines what the agent presents at each decision point.

For example, a feature workflow can pause before implementation. The agent brings you the proposed behavior, tradeoffs and a recommendation. You approve the plan, request changes or hold the work.

After approval, agents can implement and review the change against your standards. You can require another decision before release, with test results and unresolved risks as evidence.

[Spacedock Review](../review/) presents the work for your feedback and decision. Workflow defines when that review happens, what it contains and what happens next.

## Standards and trust

You and your agent can refine the standards and gate content as you learn what each decision needs. Add missing context, remove distracting detail, or change the evidence required.

You can also add decision points or explicitly delegate decisions to an agent. You control how much attention the workflow requires.

**Related guides**

- [Your first workflow](../get-started/first-workflow/): design a workflow and run its first work items.
- [Project survey](../get-started/survey/): identify the process in your existing agent history.
- [Review standards](standards/): define what good work looks like at each stage.

# Review standards

Standards define what agents must produce and check at each stage. The rules generated during [workflow design](../../running-workflows/commission/) are a starting point.

Ask your agent to refine them, or type `review stages` during workflow design for a walkthrough.

Standards define good work. [Gate content](../../concepts/gates-and-decisions/#gate-content) defines the evidence you see before a decision. You can refine both as the workflow develops.
# Workflow, use it

# Your first workflow

[Install Spacedock](../install/), then describe a repeatable piece of work and decide where it needs your judgment.

## Describe the work

```
spacedock claude "/spacedock:commission ship features through design, implementation, and review"
```

The agent asks about your work and proposes a workflow. For example:

> Each task moves through design, implementation and review.
>
> You approve the design before implementation. A separate agent reviews the result before your final decision.
>
> Requested changes return to implementation.

## Set the standards

Adjust the proposed stages, decision points and quality standards. Type `review stages` to walk through the standards with your agent.

For each decision point, specify the context and evidence you need. This is the workflow's [gate content](../../concepts/gates-and-decisions/#gate-content).

## Run the first tasks

Choose the first work items with your agent. After you accept the design and standards, the agent starts the work.

At a gate, the agent presents the evidence and asks for your decision. Approve, request changes or hold the work.

## Resume later

Run [`/spacedock:debrief`](../../running-workflows/debrief/) before you end the session.

To resume:

```
spacedock claude
```

The agent reads the workflow records and picks up the work.

**Related guides**

- [Workflow operation](../../running-workflows/operating/)
- [Project survey](../survey/): start from your existing agent history.

# Project survey

Survey reads your local agent history to identify recurring work and decisions that need your attention.

## Survey the project

In Claude Code, run:

```
/spacedock:survey
```

Survey uses [agentsview](https://agentsview.io/), a tool for reading agent session history. It asks before installing a missing dependency.

The survey is read-only. It reports:

- Repeated work and manual interventions.
- Current workstreams.
- Unresolved decisions.

## Use the findings

Your agent can propose a workflow from the findings. You decide whether to create it and which decisions remain yours.

To describe a workflow yourself, see [Your first workflow](../first-workflow/).

# Workflow design

Describe the work to your agent. It proposes stages, standards and decision points for you to adjust.

## Describe the work

In a session started with `spacedock claude`, use:

```
/spacedock:commission ship features through design, implementation, and review
```

## Review the design

You decide:

- **The work items:** what each task produces.
- **The stages:** how each task moves from an idea to completion.
- **The decision points:** where work pauses for you and where requested changes go.
- **The standards:** what agents must produce and check at each stage.

For each decision point, [gate content](../../concepts/gates-and-decisions/#gate-content) defines the context and evidence the agent presents to you.

## Refine the standards

The generated rules are a starting point. Ask your agent to refine them, or type `review stages` for a walkthrough of each stage.

## Run the workflow

After you accept the design and standards, the agent starts the first work items. [Your first workflow](../../get-started/first-workflow/) shows the full interaction.

# Session debrief

A debrief records completed work, decisions and follow-up items for the next session.

## Record the session

In Claude Code, run:

```
/spacedock:debrief
```

The agent drafts the record from Git history and workflow files. You confirm the session's scope and add context behind decisions.

## Follow-up work

Workflow improvements stay with the project. For Spacedock bugs, the agent offers to file an anonymized GitHub issue. You approve or edit each issue before it sends it.

# Workflow operation

Talk to your agent to add work, check progress and make decisions.

## Start a session

```
spacedock claude
```

The agent reads the workflow records and continues work that is ready. It coordinates workers and brings you decisions or blockers.

## Check progress

Ask questions such as:

- What needs my decision?
- What is blocked?
- What is ready next?

You can add work or change priorities in the same conversation.

## Decide at a gate

The agent presents the evidence specified by the workflow's [gate content](../../concepts/gates-and-decisions/#gate-content). You can approve, request changes or hold the work.

Your decision and feedback become part of the work item's record. The agent continues or routes the requested changes according to the workflow.

## End a session

Run [`/spacedock:debrief`](../debrief/) to record the completed work, decisions and follow-up items.

The next session reads the workflow records to resume the work.
# Concepts

# Gates and decisions

A gate pauses work for a decision. You choose which stages need gates and what evidence each gate presents.

## Gate content

Gate content defines what you need to judge the work at that stage.

| Decision                 | Useful context and evidence                    |
| ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------- |
| Approve a plan           | Proposed behavior, alternatives and tradeoffs  |
| Accept an implementation | Changes, test results and unresolved findings  |
| Release a change         | User impact, remaining risks and rollback plan |

Ask your agent to adjust the gate content as you learn what helps you decide. The instructions live in the workflow README.

## Your decision

The agent presents the work, supporting evidence and a recommendation. You can respond in the conversation or use [Spacedock Review](../../review/).

| Decision            | What happens next                                                       |
| ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Approve**         | The agent continues with the approved work                              |
| **Request changes** | The agent routes your feedback to the stage responsible for the changes |
| **Hold**            | The agent pauses the work                                               |

The workflow records your decision and its reason.

## Rejections

A review stage can send failed work back for correction before it reaches you. The reviewer then checks the revised work.

The automatic correction loop stops after three cycles and asks you how to proceed.

## Delegation

You can explicitly authorize an agent to make specified decisions. State the scope and conditions of that authority in the conversation.

The agent still presents the evidence and records the decision under its own identity.

**Related guides**

- [Workflow operation](../../running-workflows/operating/)
- [Review standards](../../workflow/standards/)

# The operating model

You define the goal, standards and decisions you retain. Your agent coordinates the work and brings those decisions to you with evidence.

## Roles

| Role              | Responsibility                                                               |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Captain**       | You set the direction and make decisions, including what to delegate         |
| **First officer** | Your coordinating agent assigns work, checks progress and presents decisions |
| **Ensign**        | A worker agent performs a stage's work and reports the result                |

## Parallel work

A workflow can run several work items at once. Each item has its own progress record and decision points.

Ask your coordinating agent what needs attention, what is blocked or what can proceed.

## Review

A separate review stage can check work against your standards. A [gate](../gates-and-decisions/) brings you the evidence for the decision you retain.

**Related guides**

- [Workflow operation](../../running-workflows/operating/)
- [Workflows and entities](../workflows-and-entities/)
- [Stage lifecycle](../stage-lifecycle/)

# The stage lifecycle

Each work item moves through the stages in your workflow. Each stage defines the work to do and the evidence required.

## A development workflow

```
flowchart LR
  design --> implementation --> review --> done
  review -. changes .-> implementation
  classDef gate stroke:#e3b04b,stroke-width:2.5px
  class design,review gate
```

In this example, the outlined stages pause for your decision: before implementation and after review.

Requested changes return to implementation. The reviewer checks the revised work before it returns to you.

## Stage settings

You can ask your agent to configure a stage to:

- Pause at a [gate](../gates-and-decisions/).
- Use a separate reviewer with fresh context.
- Return findings to the stage responsible for corrections.
- Limit concurrent work or use a specialist agent.

## Isolated work

Code stages can use separate Git worktrees so work items have their own branches and files.

**Related guides**

- [Workflow design](../../running-workflows/commission/)
- [Gates and decisions](../gates-and-decisions/)

# Workflows and entities

A workflow keeps its rules and work records as plain text in your repository. An **entity** is one work item.

## Workflow rules

The workflow README defines the stages, standards and [gate content](../gates-and-decisions/#gate-content).

Ask your agent to change these rules as you learn what the work requires. You can also edit the README directly.

## Work items

Each work item has a Markdown record with its goal, acceptance criteria, progress and stage reports. Related artifacts can live beside it.

Your agent maintains the records as work proceeds. You can read them to understand what happened or resume in another session.

## State storage

Workflow state can live in a [separate checkout](../../advanced/split-root-state/) to keep routine progress commits off your code branch.

**Related guides**

- [Workflow design](../../running-workflows/commission/)
- [Frontmatter contract](../../reference/frontmatter-contract/)
# Advanced topics

# External trackers

Your backlog can stay in GitHub Issues, Linear or another tracker.

Ask your agent to create a workflow item from an external issue. For example: “Intake GitHub issue #134.”

The workflow item keeps a reference to the source. The tracker remains the place for intake and discussion; Spacedock coordinates execution.

# Mods and standing teammates

A **mod** adds behavior to a workflow without adding a stage. Ask your agent to install an existing mod or create one.

## Lifecycle hooks

A mod can act at startup, while the workflow is idle or before work completes.

For example, the [pr-merge mod](https://github.com/spacedock-dev/spacedock/blob/main/docs/dev/_mods/pr-merge.md) manages pull requests and keeps work open until the PR merges.

## Standing teammates

A standing teammate is a specialist agent available throughout a session for recurring work.

For example, the [comm-officer mod](https://github.com/spacedock-dev/spacedock/blob/main/docs/dev/_mods/comm-officer.md) provides a prose editor for drafts and summaries.

# Multiple workflows

A project can have several workflows, each with its own stages and standards. Your agent can coordinate them in one session.

For example, one workflow can run experiments while another develops the software those experiments need.

Tell your agent about dependencies between work items so it can account for them before dispatch.

# Local plugin development

For normal setup, use [Installation](../../get-started/install/).

## Local checkout

Use `--plugin-dir <checkout>` before `--` to select a local plugin checkout.

For Claude Code and Pi, the override applies to that session and does not use the Safehouse sandbox.

For Codex, it creates a persistent installation that replaces the existing Spacedock plugin. Run the command again after changes to the checkout.

Codex does not accept `--plugin-dir` after `--`.

## Alternate marketplace

Set `SPACEDOCK_MARKETPLACE_SOURCE` to select a local or alternate marketplace:

```
SPACEDOCK_MARKETPLACE_SOURCE=/path/to/local/marketplace spacedock install --host codex
```

# Workflow refits

After a Spacedock upgrade, use `/spacedock:refit path/to/workflow` in Claude Code to update the generated workflow files.

Your agent presents a diff for each proposed change, including any migration. You decide what to apply.

# Split-root state

Split-root state keeps workflow progress commits off your code branch. Workflow rules stay with the code; work records live in a separate Git checkout.

Ask your agent to configure this layout. On a fresh clone, restore the state checkout with:

```
spacedock state init
```

Conflicting edits to the same work item stop for your decision.
# Reference

# Command reference

Run `spacedock <command> --help` for the full options. Run `spacedock` for the command list.

## Version

`spacedock --version` reports the version, platform and release channel. Inside an agent session, it also reports the runtime and sandbox.

## Launch

| Command            | Agent       |
| ------------------ | ----------- |
| `spacedock claude` | Claude Code |
| `spacedock codex`  | Codex       |
| `spacedock pi`     | Pi          |

Claude Code is the primary Workflow host. Codex and Pi support is experimental.

Launch from your project directory. You can include a task:

```
spacedock claude "continue the workflow"
```

Put agent-specific options after `--`. See [Supported sandboxes](../sandbox/) for sandbox options and [Local plugin development](../../advanced/plugin-development/) for local checkouts.

## Setup

| Command             | Purpose                                                                                            |
| ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `spacedock install` | Install or refresh the agent integration                                                           |
| `spacedock doctor`  | Check installation and compatibility                                                               |
| `spacedock update`  | Update Spacedock, Review, Compass and their plugins to the newest release on this binary's channel |

`install` and `doctor` accept `--host claude`, `--host codex` or `--host pi`. The default is Claude Code. Follow the doctor output to resolve setup problems.

See [Installation](../../get-started/install/) for the manual setup path.

## Workflow

Your agent uses these commands to operate the workflow.

| Command                 | Purpose                                                 |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `spacedock status`      | Read or update work item state                          |
| `spacedock new`         | Create a work item                                      |
| `spacedock dispatch`    | Prepare worker assignments                              |
| `spacedock gate`        | Prepare reviews, record decisions and read gate history |
| `spacedock merge guard` | Complete delivery and record the outcome                |
| `spacedock state`       | Manage the workflow state checkout                      |
| `spacedock completion`  | Generate shell completions                              |

`spacedock gate read <ref-or-path> --json` returns the stored `gates` object, including every attempt and its application state. References and paths use the same resolution as `status --read`, including archived entities. The command changes no files. Records and attempts retain their stored order. Scalar values retain their stored values. An entity without gate history returns `{"records":[],"version":1}`. Invalid gate data exits nonzero without JSON output.

```
spacedock gate read gate-history-json-reader --json --workflow-dir docs/dev
spacedock gate read archive:finished-task --json --workflow-dir docs/dev
```

See [Workflow operation](../../running-workflows/operating/) for the conversation you use to direct the work.

# Frontmatter contract

YAML frontmatter stores workflow settings and work item state. Your agent maintains these fields.

| Record          | Contents                             | Schema                                                                                                           |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Workflow README | Stages, defaults and decision points | [Workflow schema](https://github.com/spacedock-dev/spacedock/blob/main/docs/schema/workflow-readme.mdschema.yml) |
| Work item       | Identity, current stage and outcome  | [Entity schema](https://github.com/spacedock-dev/spacedock/blob/main/docs/schema/entity.mdschema.yml)            |

The schemas define field names, types and required values. [Workflows and entities](../../concepts/workflows-and-entities/) explains the files you see.

# Glossary

## Workflow

Stages, standards and decision points for a recurring type of work. See [Workflows and entities](../../concepts/workflows-and-entities/).

## Entity

One work item and its progress record. See [Workflows and entities](../../concepts/workflows-and-entities/).

## Stage

A step with defined work and standards, such as design, implementation or review. See [Stage lifecycle](../../concepts/stage-lifecycle/).

## Gate

A checkpoint that requires a decision before work continues. See [Gates and decisions](../../concepts/gates-and-decisions/).

## Gate content

The context and evidence presented at a decision point. See [Gate content](../../concepts/gates-and-decisions/#gate-content).

## First officer

The agent that coordinates workers and brings decisions to you. See [The operating model](../../concepts/operating-model/).

## Ensign

A worker agent assigned to a stage. See [The operating model](../../concepts/operating-model/).

## Mod

An extension that adds workflow behavior without adding a stage. See [Mods and standing teammates](../../advanced/mods-and-standing-teammates/).

## Standing teammate

A specialist agent available throughout a session. See [Mods and standing teammates](../../advanced/mods-and-standing-teammates/).

## Split-root state

Workflow records stored in a separate Git checkout from the code. See [Split-root state](../../advanced/split-root-state/).

# Supported sandboxes

| Sandbox                                     | Platforms | Trigger                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------------------- | --------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [`safehouse`](https://agent-safehouse.dev/) | macOS     | A `.safehouse` profile in the working directory, `--safehouse`, or any `--safehouse-*` option |

## Additional profiles

| Option                            | Type                      | Description                                     | Default |
| --------------------------------- | ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | ------- |
| `--safehouse-append-profile PATH` | Optional, repeatable path | Append a safehouse policy file for this launch. | None    |

```
spacedock claude --safehouse-append-profile=file.sb
spacedock codex --safehouse-append-profile="profiles/local rules.sb"
spacedock pi --safehouse-append-profile=first.sb --safehouse-append-profile=second.sb
```

Both `--safehouse-append-profile=PATH` and `--safehouse-append-profile PATH` select safehouse. Place the option before `--`; tokens after `--` go to the coding agent. Relative paths start in the directory where you launch Spacedock. Each occurrence supplies one path; repeats retain their order. Safehouse loads project-config profiles before these profiles, then applies its final write protections. Safehouse reports invalid profile paths or content, and Spacedock returns the failure. An existing sandbox stays active; this option still requests a safehouse launch and cannot relax the parent sandbox.
